title: Referrals and Authorizations Utilization Review: Turnaround, Pended Requests and Late Requests
content:
This chapter sets how a request under **Referrals and Authorizations** is decided once the region receives it: within what time, when it is pended, when a pended request may be denied, and which late or emergency requests are accepted.

## Section 1. Decision time

A standard request is decided within the authorization type's standard review business days, and an urgent request within the type's urgent review hours, of receipt. Business days are Monday through Friday, excluding federal holidays.

## Section 2. Pending for clinical information

Where the type requires clinical notes to accompany the request and the notes are missing, the request is pended and the requesting provider is asked for them. The patient cannot supply clinical notes on the provider's behalf by phone.

## Section 3. Denial of a pended request

A pended request is denied for missing information only once more than the type's pend period (in calendar days) has passed since the information was requested. The pend period is counted in calendar days starting the day after the date the information was requested, so the denial may be made from the day after that date plus the pend period, and not on that day itself.

- The clock starts from the date the information was requested, as recorded on the request in the system; it is that record, not anyone's recollection, that fixes the start.
- The boundary is exclusive: on the last day of the pend period the request may not yet be denied for missing information.

Information that arrives inside the pend period is reviewed and the request approved or denied on its merits.

## Section 4. Retrospective requests and emergency admissions

A retrospective request is accepted only within the type's retrospective request window (calendar days) of the service start. An emergency admission is covered without a prior request only when the facility notified the region within the type's emergency notification hours of the admission.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical dates)

Taking a type whose pend period is 14 days, with the information requested on 1 March:

| Day | Pend days counted so far | May the request be denied for missing information |
|---|---|---|
| 15 March | 14 (2 March through 15 March) | no, this is the last day of the pend period |
| 16 March | the period has passed | yes, from this day |

If the requested notes arrive on 10 March, inside the period, the request is decided on its merits instead.
